title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors & SVD
interviewAnswer: Eigenvectors are directions preserved by a linear transformation up to scaling. SVD decomposes any matrix into orthogonal directions and singular values, making it useful for compression, PCA intuition and low-rank approximation.
why: Eigenvectors/SVD underpin PCA, low-rank approximation, conditioning and many representation/compression methods.
intuition: An eigenvector is a direction a square matrix transforms without changing direction, only scale. SVD decomposes any matrix into orthogonal input/output directions with nonnegative strengths.
deepDive: For square A, Av=λv. SVD exists for any m×n matrix: A=UΣVᵀ. Singular values rank directions by how strongly the transformation acts. Truncating small singular values gives the best low-rank approximation under common norms and reveals effective dimensionality. For symmetric covariance matrices, PCA eigenvectors correspond to right singular vectors of centered data.
math:
Av=λv
A=UΣVᵀ
Rank-k approximation: A_k=U_k Σ_k V_kᵀ
workedExample: A dataset with 100 correlated features may have most variance captured by the first 10 singular directions, enabling compression or visualization.
commonMistakes: Assuming every matrix has a full set of real eigenvectors.
Using PCA without centering or considering scale.
followUps: Why does SVD work for rectangular matrices?

production: Low-rank methods reduce storage/compute and diagnose redundant representations, but truncation can remove rare yet important directions—validate downstream impact.
